ratings.reason: A declarative CIRCOS grammar with explicit terminators genuinely constrains what the generator may emit and the quote shows the grammar itself, but it is a plot-specific DSL that a designer outside genomics visualization cannot lift.

Varying which triplet elements are provided versus hidden is a real generation constraint with a pedagogical purpose, but the quote is a figure caption and the mechanism sits in the knowledge-graph annotation pipeline rather than in a visible interface rule.

Deliberately withholding whether the label follows from the reason and reframing the explanation as a question is a clean reserved-control move with measured accuracy gains, though the study manipulation rather than a shipped interface is what is specified.
The analogy design space is a taxonomy the generator is steered by, not a boundary expressed in the interface; the quote names dimensions without showing what a user does or sees.
Fixing five contextual dimensions to record is a legible output schema, but it reads as a data-collection decision for a diary agent rather than a guardrail with any user-visible control.

Presenting an intentionally incomplete S->B->A triple so the learner must supply the application is a crisp withheld-answer mechanism, clearly shown in the quote, but the biomimicry-education framing limits how directly it transfers.

User-defined evaluation criteria are a standing rule set consulted on every run and the tool is well known, but the criteria govern how outputs are judged more than what the generator may produce, so it sits closer to the evaluation dimension.

CodeAid is close to a canonical reserved-control exemplar: the system runs the pipeline that would produce code and deliberately does not emit it, the rule is the product's defining constraint, and a semester-long classroom deployment gives the outcome claim real weight.

Having the virtual classmate answer only part of a question so students can complete it is a genuinely non-obvious withholding move with a legible rule, but the VR-classroom participation setting is narrow and the effect is on engagement rather than task outcome.
The three-part risk report is a fixed output template with a real purpose, but it is a document format for a reporting tool rather than a constraint the user can see or adjust.
The refusal to hand users a per-publisher bias verdict is a defensible withheld-answer stance, but the quote is a sentence of design rationale that does not show what the interface does instead.

Standing dietary rules declared once and applied to every subsequent supermarket interaction is exactly the user-authored-rules mechanism and the scenario is concrete, though the quote is a vignette rather than a specification of how rules are entered, edited, or shown to be firing.
The listed prompt slots are an internal prompt-assembly format for a UI search tool; nothing in the quote is visible to the user as a rule or boundary.

Collaborative prototyping of LLM policies is squarely this dimension's territory and the topic is timely, but the coded quote is a definitional sentence about what policies are and shows none of PolicyPad's actual interaction, so the mechanism is unjudgeable from what is present.

Grounding writing support in writing-center pedagogy so the tool never generates verbatim text is a strong, principled instance of reserving the task for the user, though the quote states the constraint rather than showing the interaction that replaces generation.

Casting the model as a maieutic questioner that will not write on the actor's behalf is a clear reserved-control framing and the quote names the constraint explicitly, but the actor-training context and the absence of any described screen limit what a designer can rebuild.

A user-built rubric with weighted criteria in a tabular layout is both a visible template and a standing rule set, and both edges are central-high; it is competent and well-specified rather than surprising.

Expert-aligned templates that bound what meditation guidance may say is a real safety constraint, but the quote describes an internal agent pipeline and gives no user-facing expression of the boundary.
The named prompt modules are backend prompt scaffolding for Chinese-painting ideation; the constraint never reaches the interface and the structure is the default thing anyone would build.

The Product/Design System/Feature/Component hierarchy is a legible scaffold that constrains UI generation at four levels, but the quote describes a representation rather than an interaction, and hierarchical spec decomposition is now a common move.
Capping interventions at 100 words in a fixed three-part bullet structure is a study-instrument formatting decision for consistency across conditions, not a guardrail the user encounters as such.

Segmenting speech into a fixed structure and then eliciting the missing parts couples a template with a targeted withholding, which is a nice pairing, but the mechanism is described only at figure-caption level and the autistic-adolescent journaling context is specific.
Structured inter-agent data exchange is multi-agent plumbing for consistency; no boundary is expressed through the interface and nothing here is reusable as a design move.

The Explanation/Action/Artifact triple gives a nameable unit that the model must fill for each decision step, which is rebuildable, but it functions as a capture schema for workflow documentation more than as a constraint on generation.

The keynote/signal/soundmark/archetype layering shapes what the generator produces, but the quote is a system summary and the taxonomy is borrowed soundscape theory rather than an interface-level rule.

Letting users write rules that edit the explanation itself, closing the loop from interpretation back to model behaviour, is a genuinely non-obvious inversion; the quote states the proposal without showing the rule-authoring surface.
Managing a criteria set through a dedicated tab is a standing rule store, but the coded quote describes navigation chrome rather than the rules doing any constraining work.

Objectives as a small typed JSON record with a name, description, and 1-10 weight, generated on the fly per interaction, is a clean and thoroughly domain-independent way to make an ad-hoc constraint concrete and inspectable.

Treating the system prompt as an editable specification that co-evolves with a growing test set is a strong account of how a rule set actually gets maintained, though the quote is terminological and the interaction that drives the co-evolution is not shown.

A workbench for authoring and stress-testing chatbot principle sets against personas is a solid user-authored-rules instance with a comparative study behind it; the quote is a contribution statement, so the authoring surface itself stays undescribed.
Multi-policy compliance evaluation is on-topic, but the coded evidence is a model-card format, which is documentation structure rather than a constraint shaping an observable interaction.

Designers author SVG templates plus explicit design and context rules and then flip to a Test Mode to see the rules bite, which is a rebuildable authoring-and-verification loop; the facial-expression-interface domain narrows its reach.
Value alignment and reflective partnership are stated as intent; the quote offers no rule representation, no authoring step, and nothing observable, so this cannot be judged as a mechanism.

ConstraintMaker puts output constraints in a graphical interface and guarantees conformance, which is about as literal an instance of this dimension as the shortlist contains and it transfers to any structured-generation task; as a short late-breaking paper the evidence behind the guarantee is thin.
Ten fixed metadata fields for a museum-artifact corpus is data schema design, not an interface constraint, and it does not leave its collection.
The Case History Taking Template is a legible sectioned document the model must fill, but it is a clinical form applied in the obvious way.
An object/space class hierarchy bounding what the LLM may instantiate in a game world is a real generation constraint, but it is engine architecture with no user-visible rule surface.
Adapting an existing personalized-learning framework's dimensions as prompt structure is the default first thing to build and the quote shows no interaction.
Reusable song blueprints as structural templates for lyric generation is concretely described, but the conference-karaoke application makes any impact claim hard to take seriously.

A mandated three-step response pattern (acknowledge, normalize, offer structured next step) is a genuine behavioural guardrail for a sensitive population and is rebuildable verbatim, though it is a scripted response format rather than anything the user controls.
Four linked components mapping pedagogy to gameplay is described only as a structure; without the authoring interaction there is nothing a designer can lift.

Constraining conversational scoring to the original instrument's response anchors is a precise, checkable guardrail that keeps a free-form interview commensurable with validated measurement, and it transfers to any survey or rating task; the constraint is enforced in the pipeline rather than shown to the participant.

A strict DSL that prevents the model from emitting arbitrary structures or commands is a properly stated guardrail with a security-flavoured rationale and it transfers to any generate-into-a-runtime setting; the quote asserts the prevention without describing the DSL or the interface.

Compiling design constraints into answer-set-programming rules with defined constraint semantics makes the boundary formal and machine-checkable rather than advisory, which is a genuinely interesting stance; the visualization design-space framing and the absence of any user-facing constraint editor in the quote hold it back.
Generating follow-ups against the STAR frame is a clear and portable output template, but adopting a standard interview framework as a slot set is the obvious move.
A scenario-structuring framework with LLM-assisted expansion; the quote asserts structural consistency is maintained without saying by what, so there is no mechanism to rebuild.

Pre-configured CTML constraints that the user can extend with custom requirements before generation is a well-formed constraint-authoring step with sensible defaults, precisely located in the interface by the quote, if not conceptually surprising.
Puzzle groups specified by structured templates plus constraint rules is a legible generator-bounding scheme, but it is tied to the cognitive-training activity format and shows no user-facing rule.

Fixing user actions, system events, and context as the base construction unit is a reasonable scaffold for design reasoning, but the quote is a design requirement rather than a realized interface constraint.
Forcing every podcast segment into a question-and-answer shape is a concrete and slightly non-obvious structural constraint, but it is a content format for one news application.

ConstitutionMaker turns per-output critique into persisted principles that govern every later generation, which is the user-authored-rules mechanism in its purest and most transferable form; the quote states the conversion clearly even if the elicitation UI is not shown.

Replacing the chat box with a filled-in template as the primary interaction is a clean, fully portable structural constraint that any designer can rebuild, though the reflection-support payoff is asserted rather than demonstrated in the coded evidence.
Competency-question patterns constrain generated ontology axioms in a specified way, but the mechanism is inherited from prior work and confined to ontology engineering.

Storyboard, Data Model, and GUI Skeleton as named intermediate representations that scaffold and bound code generation is concrete and inspectable; it is a well-executed version of a now-familiar IR strategy.
Tree serialization schemes for GUI layouts is model-side representation work; the constraint never becomes something the user sees or sets.
A controlled annotation list bounds the labels applied to code segments, which is a mild vocabulary constraint inside an evaluation pipeline rather than a design move.

The four-dimension reasoning structure is a prompt condition in a controlled comparison, not an interface the authors built out; useful as evidence that structure changes exploration, weak as an exemplar.

The protocol tree with answer-dependent question relevance is a decent conditional template, but the withheld-answer edge rests on a quote citing prior work rather than describing RDoFlow's own behaviour, so that half of the coding is unsupported.

Operationalizing the Paul-Elder elements as interactive slots the user works through is rebuildable and portable to other reasoning tasks, but importing an established framework as the template is the expected approach.

Modelling each preference as a named predicate over candidate solutions gives the most precisely rebuildable constraint mechanism on this list, with an actual solver behind it; it loses ground only because scheduling is a domain where constraints were already the standard framing.
Passing a JSON schema in the prompt to bound XR scene generation is clearly stated and does keep the model in-bounds, but schema-in-prompt is the baseline technique rather than a design contribution.

Bounding summary claims to a typed L1-L3 element vocabulary as a hallucination guard is a real and transferable use of a template as a safety constraint, though the elements are illustrated for authors rather than surfaced to readers.
Selecting a predefined template by topic is the plainest possible form of this pattern and the quote adds nothing beyond that.
Returning a JSON object with an answer plus follow-up questions is ordinary response formatting; there is no boundary and nothing reserved.
The 6-tuple data fact is a precise formalism, but it is an internal representation for narrative playback with no interface expression of any constraint.

Graphologue is an influential system, but its contribution is response visualization; the coded quote covers entity extraction for diagramming and shows no rule or reserved region, so it is a poor instance of this dimension.

Semantic Commit is the strongest thing here: intent specifications are an explicit user-authored rule store, and the conflict check deliberately surfaces problems while withholding the fix so the user keeps the decision, a tension most systems resolve by just auto-editing.

Grounding generated intents in attribute and intent-type taxonomies bounds the output space usefully, but the taxonomy operates inside an automated evaluation pipeline rather than as a visible constraint.

Instructors extend AI-suggested metrics with external standards and their own additions, forming a rubric that governs subsequent grading; solid but a conventional instance, and the quote is a truncated feature list.

Building a disambiguation tree whose levels correspond to taxonomy facets is a well-specified structural constraint with a clear on-screen consequence, and clarification before answering is adjacent to reserving the answer; the taxonomy itself is corpus-derived and specific.

Policy Projector lets a practitioner draw regions over observed model behaviour and attach if-then rules that act on outputs, giving both the map and the enforcement in one legible interface; it is the clearest picture on this list of what authoring a guardrail actually looks like.
Three configurable widget types bound what a prompted mobile prototype can become, which is concrete and on-screen, but the constraint reads as a prototyping palette rather than a guardrail.

Specifying that the model return CSS animation code with an explanation per snippet is a plainly described output contract that makes the results editable, but it is prompt-level formatting in a design probe.
Six feedback sections mirroring the think-aloud process is a straightforward template lifted from prior literature, with no user control over it.

CounterQuill refuses to generate the reply and teaches the user to write it instead, a clear reservation of the task for the user; the quote states the stance but not the interaction that carries the teaching.

Interview and diary study of what users expect from notification summaries; the coded quote reports strategies participants used in their own prompts, not a rule mechanism in an interface the authors built.
ratings.disqualify_reason: Interview and diary study of what users expect from notification summaries; the coded quote reports strategies participants used in their own prompts, not a rule mechanism in an interface the authors built.

ratings.reason: The typed issue/position node vocabulary constrains what the facilitation agent may add to the shared map, which is at least visible, but the quote is an interface inventory rather than a statement of any boundary.
A five-section research outline panel the model fills is a clear template, but it is a form, and nothing about it is reserved or enforced.
A derived node-and-edge schema shapes the generated concept graph, but the schema is pre-study-derived and internal; the quote shows no rule the designer sets or sees.

Structuring generated clinical reports around primary-care information themes embeds stakeholder needs in the output, which matters clinically, but the constraint is a prompt-side template with no interface presence.
Representing each instruction as an operation/parameter/object tuple bounds what the automation may emit, but this is standard action-representation plumbing for UI agents.
